title: Metcash Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Team Members
tiers.description: All directors, employees, contractors and consultants of Metcash. Subject to the insider trading ban, the Front Page Test, the short-term/speculative dealing and short-selling bans, and the hedging/derivative ban on unvested or holding-locked incentive plan Securities.

tiers.name: Directors, GLT and Specified Management
tiers.description: Directors, the Group Leadership Team and Specified Managers collectively; subject to Closed Periods (1 October/1 April to results announcement, plus Board-specified periods) and the prior written approval regime for dealing during a prohibited period.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Metcash Limited; approved by the Chair (or the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee for the Chair's own dealings); must advise the Company Secretary of margin call loan financing and notify the Company Secretary promptly after any trade.

tiers.name: GLT
tiers.description: Group Leadership Team (the Group CEO and determined direct reports); approved by the Chair; must advise the Company Secretary of margin call loan financing (register maintained), but no express post-trade notification duty is stated (unlike Directors).

tiers.name: Specified Management
tiers.description: Persons likely to have access to material information by virtue of role, including subsidiary directors/company secretaries, General Manager level and above, direct support staff of Directors/GLT, and Finance, Risk and Assurance, Legal, Corporate Affairs and Investor Relations staff. Approved by the Group CEO; no margin loan register obligation is stated for this tier.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may influence or be influenced by a Director, GLT member or Specified Manager (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants), and a company or other entity the Director, GLT member or Specified Manager can control.

definitions.hedging_definition: a hedging or other derivative transaction in connection with Securities: (a) acquired under any executive or employee incentive plan prior to vesting; or (b) whilst they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any executive or employee incentive plan

rules.detail: 'Securities' is defined as Metcash shares, options, notes, performance rights, debentures and other securities on issue or granted by Metcash; a third-party (e.g. bank-written) OTC derivative is not itself 'Securities'. Section 6.1's hedging/derivative ban is expressly limited to unvested or holding-locked incentive plan Securities, so an OTC put/call over fully vested, unrestricted shares is not reached by the deal-in-Securities regime (Closed Periods, approval) or by section 6.1.

exemption_authority: Only for dealing during a prohibited period (section 3.1): the Chair of Metcash Limited (Directors/GLT), the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee (for the Chair's own dealings) or the Group CEO (Specified Managers) may grant approval only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order/undertaking or family settlement) and only if the applicant holds no inside information. The Approver need not give reasons, may impose conditions, and may revoke approval at any time without reason; any refusal or revocation must be kept confidential. No exemption authority is stated for the section 6.1 hedging/derivative ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means all Metcash shares, options, notes, performance rights, debentures and other securities on issue or granted from time to time
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because 'Securities' is limited to instruments Metcash itself issues or grants, a bank-written OTC put or call is not 'Securities' under this policy; over vested, unrestricted shares such a derivative falls outside the Closed Period, approval and short-term dealing rules entirely, since section 6.1's hedging/derivative ban is the only provision reaching derivatives and it is expressly confined to unvested or holding-locked incentive securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to incentive-plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Team Members must not enter into a hedging or other derivative transaction in connection with Securities: (a) acquired under any executive or employee incentive plan prior to vesting; or (b) whilst they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any executive or employee incentive plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban does not reach ordinary on-market vested shares, or plan shares once vesting and any holding lock have ended, so a collar over such shares is not prohibited by this clause.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan disclosure limited to acquisition financing, Directors/GLT only
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the GLT who finance acquisitions of Securities by margin call loans must advise the Company Secretary of these arrangements
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The disclosure/register obligation is worded around financing new acquisitions and applies only to Directors and GLT, not Specified Management or other Team Members; it is unclear whether a loan secured on already-held vested shares (rather than financing a purchase) triggers the same obligation, so the bank should seek voluntary disclosure or Board sign-off for certainty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank ever enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that sale is excluded from the short-term dealing, Closed Period and outside-period rules, though it remains subject to the insider trading law generally.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approver may request more information from the applicant, grant the request, refuse the request or impose conditions on the dealing. ... If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a dealing does require approval (e.g. a collar entered while shares remain locked, or during a prohibited period), the Approver can impose bespoke conditions on the collar's terms and can revoke a granted approval at any time without reason.

summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted Metcash shares appears largely unrestricted by this policy: 'Securities' is defined narrowly as Metcash's own shares, options, notes, performance rights and debentures, so a bank-written OTC put and call are not 'Securities' and fall outside the Closed Period, approval and short-term dealing rules; the only hedging/derivative prohibition (section 6.1) is expressly confined to Securities that are unvested or still subject to a holding lock under an incentive plan. The loan leg is also workable: Directors and GLT members who finance acquisitions of Securities by margin call loans need only advise the Company Secretary for a register (with the Chair told of any lender intention to sell) rather than seek approval, though it is unclear whether this notification duty extends to a loan secured on already-vested shares rather than financing a purchase, and it does not extend to Specified Management at all. If the shares remain subject to a holding lock, or dealing occurs within a Closed Period (1 October to half-year results; 1 April to full-year results) or another Board-specified restricted period, prior written approval from the Chair (or the Group CEO for Specified Managers) is required, and is discretionary, conditional and revocable without reason. A secured lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the short-term dealing and Closed Period rules. Overall, once shares are vested and unrestricted, this policy permits a funded collar with only light-touch disclosure, making it comparatively more accommodating than policies with a broader dealing/derivatives definition.
